subject.name: Auditable Independent-Future Challenge
subject.working_paper_title: Auditable Tests for Information from Future Random Events: A Causal, Cryptographic, and Anytime-Valid Protocol

executive_summary.one_sentence: AIFC is a fail-closed evidence protocol for testing whether an exact witness irreversibly frozen before a target exists contains more information about a later independently generated random target than any admitted forward-causal model permits.
executive_summary.problem: Claims of prediction, precognition, retrocausal information or future-bit pre-existence are easily mimicked by leakage, shared causes, target pre-generation, multiple guesses, post-selection, optional stopping, rollback, forked logs, stale signatures, compromised entropy sources or self-certifying simulators.
executive_summary.proposed_solution: Require exact pre-target identity plus independently supported conditional unpredictability, causal isolation, immutable temporal ordering, multiplicity accounting, anytime-valid statistics, external freshness and fault-model-derived witness quorum before an event may be graded as incompatible with the specified forward-causal null.
executive_summary.scientific_value_if_null: Even if every physical experiment returns NULL, AIFC remains useful as a reproducible methodology for preventing false future-information claims and for auditing experiments that depend on future randomness.

core_scientific_question: Can an exact witness frozen before target generation contain information about a later certified random target beyond the history-wise guessing probability allowed by a declared forward-causal null model?

formal_core.freeze_view: Let F_{i-1} denote all information available before target T_i is generated.
formal_core.candidate_set: Freeze C_i as an F_{i-1}-measurable candidate set with |C_i| <= K_i before T_i exists.
formal_core.historywise_point_guess_bound: Require max_t P(T_i=t | F_{i-1}) <= p_i almost surely.
formal_core.sequential_bound: P(exists i<=N with T_i in C_i) <= 1 - product_i(1-a_i).

anytime_valid_eprocess.null_property: E[E_n | forward-null] <= 1 in the test-supermartingale sense

formal_core.exact_match_independent_future_no_go: If B_R is fixed from freeze-time information V_R and H_min(T|V_R)>=h, then P(B_R=T)<=2^-h. In particular, guaranteed non-degenerate exact equality cannot coexist with positive conditional min-entropy under the admitted classical forward-null.
formal_core.causal_isolation_gate: In a correctly specified Markovian DAG, require T_hard d-separated from PRE_RETURN hard view R conditional only on declared public metadata M; otherwise structural independence is not certified.
formal_core.freshness_gate: Hash chains and signatures authenticate presented history but do not by themselves prove that a later valid state was not rolled back. At least one freshness root must exist outside the rollback domain.
formal_core.witness_quorum_gate: With n witnesses and at most f Byzantine, conflicting q-certificates are excluded when 2q > n+f, equivalently q >= floor((n+f)/2)+1.

evidence_stack.purpose: A missing evidence premise never silently degrades into a physical claim.

sequential_adaptive_v0_6.important_falsifier: Marginal/average entropy can fail under adaptive history; the history-wise bound is required.

anytime_valid_v0_7.important_falsifier: Using false marginal caps a1=a2=1/2 in a correlated future process produced threshold-crossing probability 0.5 at nominal alpha=0.25; using the correct history-wise a2=1 repaired validity.

important_falsifiers: A shared latent seed creates dependence without any directed T->R or R->T path.
Conditioning on a selection collider can raise p_guess from 0.5 to 1.0.

safe_public_claims.short: I developed AIFC (Auditable Independent-Future Challenge), a candidate-novel, fail-closed protocol for rigorously testing claims that information about a future random event existed before that event was generated.
safe_public_claims.technical: AIFC combines pre-target exact-bit commitments, post-freeze certified randomness, history-wise conditional min-entropy, causal d-separation, multiplicity accounting, anytime-valid e-processes, external anti-rollback freshness and Byzantine witness quorums. Its end-to-end verifier is machine-hardened against declared attack classes; physical retrocausality has not been observed.
safe_public_claims.researcher_profile: Independent researcher developing proof-carrying, adversarial scientific protocols; creator of AIFC and JANUS evidence-first experimental methods.
forbidden_overclaims: AIFC is proven to be the first protocol of its kind worldwide.
A 256-bit match would automatically prove a retrocausal mechanism.

application_domains: computer-security experiments involving temporal ordering and immutable evidence

external_bench_blueprint.trusted_computing_base_goal: Remove Genesis from target generation and minimize its role to an open verifier/reference implementation.
external_bench_blueprint.pre_return: Freeze exact candidate bytes and obtain a q-of-n certificate from genuinely independent witness failure domains.
external_bench_blueprint.target: Generate the hard target only after the freeze using an external, publicly verifiable or independently audited randomness source.
external_bench_blueprint.hard_target_example: T = SHA256(beacon_randomness || run_id || PRE_RETURN_hash || frozen_protocol_id), with the exact derivation frozen before the selected future pulse exists.
external_bench_blueprint.analysis: Use the history-wise a_i cap and frozen e-process; report every registered run including NULLs.
external_bench_blueprint.interpretation_of_threshold_crossing: Reject the specified forward-null-or-an-evidence-premise at the stated level; do not infer a retrocausal mechanism until leakage, entropy, timing, provenance and replication alternatives survive independent audit.
